blocks.text: Burtonesque is an aesthetic and art style heavily influenced by the work and art of filmmaker Tim Burton. It is characterized by gothic visuals, a dark color palette, chaotic lines and grotesque themes, alongside Burton's signature character design.
It was created by Tim Burton during the 1980s. At the time, he was making short films while working at Walt Disney Productions

Burton's artwork is inspired by German Expressionism and Gothic revivalism, and includes aspects of both styles, in addition to a whimsical sense of surrealism and exaggerated proportions. Characters in Burton's work, and in Burtonesque art by extension, often have long, slender limbs, huge eyes with heavy eyelids and dark eyebags underneath, wispy and disheveled hair, sunken in cheeks and pale skin. The linework is often scratchy, chaotic and thin. In keeping with the Gothic theme, the color palette of Burtonesque is typically dark, utilizing black, gray, white, and shades of blue, but sometimes there will be pops of color that starkly contrasts with the rest of the scene.
